tools.description: Read a Google Sheets spreadsheet's structure: its title, locale and every sheet (tab) with its ID and grid size. The spreadsheet_id comes from drive_list_files, search_workspace or sheets_create_spreadsheet; for cell values use sheets_read_sheet_values. Returns spreadsheet_id, title, locale, spreadsheet_time_zone (the file's own setting), url, named_ranges (name, named_range_id, A1 range) and sheets, each with sheet_id, title, index, type, row_count, column_count, frozen_row_count, frozen_column_count and hidden. With include_grid_data each sheet also has values (rows of displayed cell text) and values_start (the cell of values[0][0]), else both are null.

include_grid_data.description: Also return each sheet's cell values, as displayed, in sheets[].values; this can be very large, so limit it with ranges. For values alone use sheets_read_sheet_values.

ranges.description: A1 ranges that limit the response to the sheets (and, with include_grid_data, the cells) they cover, e.g. ['Sheet1!A1:C10']; basic A1 notation as in sheets_read_sheet_values, so a bare sheet name is rejected. Omitted, every sheet is returned.

spreadsheet_id.description: Google Sheets spreadsheet ID: the Drive file ID, also the long ID in the spreadsheet's URL.

tools.description: Read the cell values of one or more A1 ranges of a Google Sheets spreadsheet in a single call. The spreadsheet_id comes from drive_list_files, search_workspace or sheets_create_spreadsheet; for the sheet (tab) names and sizes use sheets_get_spreadsheet, and to write cells sheets_update_sheet_values. Returns spreadsheet_id, count and value_ranges, one per requested range in request order (a list even for one range), each with range (the A1 range actually read), major_dimension, values (rows, or columns with major_dimension COLUMNS, without trailing empty rows and cells; [] when the range is empty) and row_count.

date_time_render_option.description: How dates and times are returned when value_render_option is not FORMATTED_VALUE: SERIAL_NUMBER (days since 1899-12-30) or FORMATTED_STRING.

major_dimension.description: Whether values are returned as a list of ROWS or a list of COLUMNS.

ranges.description: One or more ranges to read, e.g. ['Sheet1!A1:C10'] or ['Sheet1!A1:C10', 'Sheet2!A:B']. Basic A1 notation with an optional sheet prefix: 'Sheet1!A1:C10', 'A1', 'A:C' (whole columns) or '1:5' (whole rows); quote sheet names that contain spaces ('My Sheet'!A1:B2). A bare sheet name or an open-ended range such as A2:C is rejected, and without a prefix the first sheet is used.

spreadsheet_id.description: Google Sheets spreadsheet ID: the Drive file ID, also the long ID in the spreadsheet's URL.

value_render_option.description: How cell values are returned: FORMATTED_VALUE as displayed, UNFORMATTED_VALUE as raw numbers, or FORMULA to return formulas instead of results.

count.description: Number of items in this response.

tools.title: Sheets Read Sheet Values

tools.description: Write values into one A1 range of a Google Sheets spreadsheet, overwriting the cells it covers. To add rows below existing data use sheets_append_sheet_values, and for formatting or tab changes use sheets_batch_update_spreadsheet (extended tool tier); the spreadsheet_id comes from drive_list_files, search_workspace or sheets_create_spreadsheet. Returns status ok, spreadsheet_id, updated_range, updated_rows, updated_columns, updated_cells and updated_values (the written cells with include_values_in_response, else null).

include_values_in_response.description: Also return the written cells, as stored after parsing, in updated_values.

range_a1.description: Range to write. Basic A1 notation with an optional sheet prefix: 'Sheet1!A1:C10', 'A1', 'A:C' (whole columns) or '1:5' (whole rows); quote sheet names that contain spaces ('My Sheet'!A1:B2). A bare sheet name or an open-ended range such as A2:C is rejected, and without a prefix the first sheet is used.

spreadsheet_id.description: Google Sheets spreadsheet ID: the Drive file ID, also the long ID in the spreadsheet's URL.

value_input_option.description: How values are interpreted: USER_ENTERED parses them as if typed into the UI (formulas, numbers, dates); RAW stores them exactly as given, so a string such as '=SUM(A1:A3)' stays text.

values.description: Rows written from the range's top-left cell, each a list of cell values, e.g. [['Name', 'Total'], ['Ana', 42]]; they must fit inside range_a1, a null skips a cell and an empty string clears it.

due_min.description: Lower bound for the due date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or RFC3339; a time without offset is read as UTC.

show_assigned.description: Also return tasks assigned to the user, for example from Google Docs or Chat spaces.

show_completed.description: Return completed tasks too (default); false lists only open tasks. Tasks completed in the Google Tasks apps also need show_hidden true.

show_deleted.description: Also return deleted tasks, flagged deleted true.

show_hidden.description: Also return hidden tasks: completed tasks cleared from the list, including those completed in the Google Tasks apps.

tools.description: Change an existing task: edit its fields, mark it done (status 'completed') or reopen it, move it within its list (parent, previous, move_to_top) or to another list (destination_tasklist_id). Only what you pass changes and at least one change is required; a move runs first, then the field changes on the list the task ends up in. Returns status 'ok' and task, shaped as in tasks_list_tasks: id, title, status, due_date, is_overdue, completed_at, updated_at, notes_snippet, notes_truncated, parent_id, deleted, hidden and url. Flagging the task deleted asks the user to confirm first.

completed.description: Completion time to record, RFC3339 (YYYY-MM-DD means midnight UTC), usually with status 'completed'; omitted there, it defaults to now in the account time zone.

deleted.description: True flags the task as deleted (it then lists only with show_deleted), after the user confirms, like tasks_delete_task; false clears the flag.

destination_tasklist_id.description: Task list ID to move the task into, at its top level; to place it there, call again on that list with parent or previous.

due.description: New due date as YYYY-MM-DD (sent as midnight UTC) or RFC3339; Google Tasks keeps only the date.

hidden.description: Sets the hidden flag (true for completed tasks cleared from the list); Google documents it as read-only, so it may be ignored.

move_to_top.description: True moves the task to the first position at the top level of its list; not allowed with parent, previous or destination_tasklist_id.

notes.description: New details text, replacing the old notes.

parent.description: Moves the task under this task of the same list as a subtask; a move without it puts the task at the top level. Not allowed with destination_tasklist_id.

previous.description: Moves the task right after this sibling task; a move without it puts the task first among its siblings. Not allowed with destination_tasklist_id.

status.description: 'completed' marks the task done, recording completed (now in the account time zone when completed is omitted); 'needsAction' reopens it.

task_id.description: Task ID, from tasks_list_tasks, tasks_tasks_digest or tasks_create_task results.

tasklist_id.description: Task list ID from tasks_list_tasklists; omit for the account's default list.
